title: Enabling Token-wise Importance Sampling in Off-Policy RLVR with Proximal KL Regularization
data_curation: Math-only RLVR with a binary boxed-answer verifier (+1 correct, -1 incorrect/invalid in the periodic-refresh runs). Periodic-refresh experiments train on DAPO-Math-17K. Controlled-staleness experiments train on 9,453 prompts derived from FRPO's filtered DAPO-Math data; all 4B runs in that setting add DAPO-style dynamic sampling, discarding prompt groups with identical rewards and resampling to fill the batch (same rule for all methods). No new dataset is built; the contribution is the off-policy update rule.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is single-stage RL from Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B-Base (Qwen3-32B uses a post-trained checkpoint because no base was available), with no initial-model KL. The only schedule is the proximal reference refresh: the reference pi_k is frozen for L optimizer updates (L=16 for Proximal KL vs 32 for GRPO in periodic refresh; every global batch under controlled staleness), so the KL penalizes per-round movement while allowing cumulative drift from initialization. Off-policyness comes from rollout weights synced only every 64 updates, or from AReaL-style asynchronous generation at staleness 4 or 16 with 4 minibatches per batch.
method: Proximal KL separates the proximal reference pi_k (the improvement target, objective E[R] - beta*KL(pi_theta||pi_k)) from the logged behavior policy that generated each response. The loss multiplies a detached single-token importance weight pi_theta/pi_behav by (group advantage minus future KL credit C), where C sums beta*clip(log pi_theta/pi_k, +-eps_F) over the current token and up to H-1 future tokens, and drops PPO clipping entirely (Adam, grad-norm clip 1). Theory: under coverage and local-expressiveness assumptions, full-tail future KL credit with token-wise weights has the exact Gibbs proximal optimizer as its unique stationary policy for any stale behavior mixture, without a critic or sequence-level ratio products. The paper also gives tabular continuous-time convergence and a finite-sample reward guarantee for linear logistic models. Working default: H=full, beta=0.30, eps_F=0.05 (H=32 suggested for 4B). Baselines are decoupled-reference GRPO (eps_clip=0.2), CISPO (IS-weight clip [0,5]) and unclipped PG.
eval_metrics: Held-out: greedy pass@1 on MATH500, OlympiadBench, MinervaMath and Gaokao2023MathEn; mean@16 on AIME24/25 and AMC23/24, plus AIME24 pass@16 curves. The headline metric is a micro-averaged Average over 4,149 responses (three seeds at 1.7B). Training accuracy under periodic refresh is tracked at 1.7B-32B. Headline: 1.7B off-policy Average reaches 33.00-33.18 vs GRPO's 32.14-32.41 at LR 5e-6, and 32.97 vs 30.39 at LR 1e-5 with staleness 4. 4B reaches 48.13/48.35 vs 47.17/46.13 at staleness 4/16. The on-policy comparison is roughly a tie (34.09 vs 34.50). Diagnostics include policy entropy, pre-clip gradient norm and fixed-policy correction variance V(H).
key_results: Proximal KL beats GRPO on micro-averaged accuracy in all seven matched off-policy settings (Qwen3-1.7B/4B, two learning rates, staleness 0/4/16), by up to +2.58 points. Moving from staleness 4 to 16, its 4B Average rises (+0.22) while GRPO's falls (-1.04). Under periodic refresh it avoids the PG/CISPO collapses at 8B/32B, and 8B reaches 50% training accuracy in about 200 updates versus about 640 for GRPO.
evolution_note: The paper builds on GRPO/DAPO token-wise ratios, batch-size-invariant PPO's split of the proximal and behavior policies (as used in AReaL and AsyncWebRL), the same group's FRPO Future-KL gradient identity, and PCL/Trust-PCL soft path consistency. It reacts to the growing off-policyness of asynchronous RLVR systems (AReaL, Slime, Miles) and to the bias of PPO clipping and CISPO-style weight clipping. It offers a theoretically grounded, critic-free alternative in which bounded future-KL feedback replaces the clip gate.
